name: apply 2 — AI review: advisory first read of every new application

nodes.name: Review schedule
nodes.notes: Runs on SWEEP_CRON, and apply 1a and 1b also call this workflow directly when they have created rows. The stage filter (applied to reviewed) keeps a row to one model call across sweeps. The claim below is what keeps two runs of the same minute from both paying for it.

nodes.name: Ask the reviewer model
nodes.notes: Scaleway Generative APIs (EU), OpenAI-compatible — provider swappable via AI_BASE_URL. The call is advisory and read-only, so it is deliberately not behind the DRY_RUN gate.

nodes.notes: apply 1a and apply 1b call this when they have created rows, so a new application is reviewed in the same pass rather than waiting for the next sweep. The schedule above is the safety net: a hand-off that never arrives costs one sweep interval, not an application.

nodes.name: Claimable for review?
nodes.notes: A row another run is already working is skipped. A claim older than STALE_CLAIM_MINUTES (30 when unset) is treated as abandoned, so a run that died cannot strand an application forever.

nodes.name: Claim the row for review
nodes.notes: A compare-and-swap, not a hopeful write. The second condition is the value this run just read, null included, so only one of several runs can match. A conditional update that matches nothing returns an empty result and emits no items, which silently skips the row. The model call sits downstream of this node, so a row is never paid for twice.

nodes.notes: Fire and forget. It never waits and it never fails this workflow, so a verdict is written and posted whatever happens downstream. apply 3 reads the rows itself, so nothing is passed. Its own schedule still covers a hand-off that is lost.
